I have been farming for 60 years. I am 70 now, and I only finished primary school, but I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and calculate costs. My family has 16.9 mu of good flat land in Quzhou, all in wheat-maize rotation. There are three of us at home — me, my wife, and my son. We have our own well for irrigation, which is important because rain alone is never enough here.

For **winter wheat**, I will rotary till the land before sowing in October. I use improved wheat seed, about 30 jin per mu — that is half a bag. I learned long ago that planting too deep or too shallow costs yield, so I set the machine carefully. For base fertilizer, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 100 jin — the kind the dealer sells for wheat, with more phosphorus in it. Then in spring, when the wheat turns green, I topdress with urea. I put 50 to 60 jin per mu. I would rather put a bit too much than see the wheat turn yellow and lose grain. Fertilizer costs money, but a bad harvest is a disaster. I irrigate three times: once after sowing for winter survival, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray three times — herbicide once after emergence, insecticide once in spring, and fungicide once if the weather turns humid. I expect about 480 kg per mu if frost does not damage it.

For **summer maize**, after the wheat harvest in early June, I plant directly without tilling. Everyone around here does no-tillage for maize — it saves time and diesel, and the wheat stubble keeps moisture. I use hybrid maize seed, one package per mu, about 2.5 kg. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, the high-nitrogen kind meant for maize. When the maize reaches the big trumpet stage, if it looks pale, I spread another 30 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once after sowing if the soil is dry, and once at grain filling. I spray twice: herbicide once early, insecticide once when the borers come. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

I watch what my neighbors do. If most people around me apply a certain amount, I do the same — I do not want to take risks. With 16.9 mu, I am not the biggest farmer, but I am not small either. I hire a combine for harvest, but fertilizing and spraying I mostly do myself. Every yuan matters, but going hungry matters more.
